study_note: Four Humanoid Walk state backbone configurations compare native direct-clipped versus smooth tanh log-standard-deviation mappings with shared [-10, 2] bounds, crossed with corrected post-tanh entropy targets -21 and -10.5 joint nats. All use automatic alpha initialized at 1, no actor Q normalization, mean-pair actor Q, min-pair target Q, entropy-augmented critics, and stochastic prior-only collection without inner optimization or MPPI. Native random network initialization is preserved: matched seeds match raw weights, not initial action distributions across mappings. Each configuration runs seeds 55 and 56 for 2 million decisions with 80 scheduled checkpoints every 25,000 decisions. This is an exploratory two-seed screen, not confirmatory evidence. Algorithm files specify complete settings; the manifest does not override alg_params.
